Payday 2 is one of the best cooperative heist games ever made. More than a decade after its release, it still offers an enormous amount of content, deep progression, and thrilling teamwork. While it has some rough edges, its replayability is exceptional.

What it does well
Outstanding co-op gameplay. Planning and executing heists with friends is the game's biggest strength. Whether you choose stealth or go in guns blazing, teamwork is essential.
Huge variety of heists. Banks, jewelry stores, casinos, prisons, and even over-the-top missions inspired by action movies keep the gameplay fresh.
Deep customization. Hundreds of weapons, masks, attachments, perks, and skill builds let you tailor your playstyle.
Excellent replayability. Randomized objectives and multiple difficulty levels make the same heist feel different each time.
Weaknesses
Steep learning curve. New players can feel overwhelmed by the many mechanics, skills, and menus.
Aging visuals. The graphics and animations show their age compared to modern shooters.
Large amount of DLC. Although many editions bundle content together, the game's DLC history can make it confusing to know what's included.
Public matchmaking can be inconsistent. Playing with friends is generally a much better experience.
Gameplay

The core loop is simple but addictive:

Case the target.
Attempt a stealthy robbery or prepare for a loud assault.
Complete objectives while police escalate their response.
Escape with the loot.

Stealth requires careful coordination, while loud gameplay becomes a frantic survival challenge against increasingly aggressive police forces.

Who should play it?
Yes, if you enjoy cooperative shooters, teamwork, progression systems, and replayable missions.
Maybe not, if you mainly play solo or prefer story-driven campaigns.
Overall

Payday 2 remains a benchmark for co-op heist games. Despite its age, few games match its blend of planning, action, customization, and replay value.

Overa…

I really want to love this game as I, as do many people, have or had a love-hate relationship with the game ever since the horrible launch that ruined its reputation. Obviously they've fixed many of those issues, like the servers, the revamping the UI, introduction of skills 2.0, remaking the core heists, and making it more enjoyable for new players to get into the game. But it is not without the issues that still exist.

When you lose connection while joining a match, it send you back to the menu for some reason. Skills 2.0 really encourages grenades for some reason, I get that grenades were not really a central part of payday, but in every skill tree section there are grenade skills that can genuinely just outclass your guns. Also the way the skills are formatted in skills 2.0 doesn't really coincide with the other skills that you want to make. Like why is the medic bag skill tree in CONMAN instead of SOLDIER? There are skills there higher up in the skill tree that I could've gotten, but cant because I need a higher amount of points invested in CONMAN now instead of SOLDIER,

The game still has issues, but guess what? I'm genuinely starting to like PAYDAY 2 as an actual game now. Not out of pity, not out of obligation, but genuine interest and passion that I have for this franchise. I'd say you should play it again if you bought the game at launch, or buy it when it's on sale, since its a enjoyable experience..

With the direction that this game is going, they make improvements little by little and hopefully this game can age like PAYDAY 1 did

Honestly really fun game, especially if you have a group of friends to play with. There is a crazy amount of content here and so many different heists to do, from quick store robberies to massive multi-day bank jobs. The soundtrack goes absolutely hard too and makes the loud phases feel so much more intense. Plus the gunplay feels great and there are a ton of different skills and perk decks so you can pretty much build your character however you want.My only major complaint is that the menus and inventory system feel super outdated and clunky. It takes a long time to learn where everything is, and trying to modify weapons or sort through gear feels like a chore when you are a new player. The game is also really bad at explaining things to beginners. When you start out, you're kind of just thrown in and you don't really know what to do in some heists, so you end up wandering around confused while the cops swarm you unless someone carries you through it. They really need to update the UI and give it a clean overhaul to make it easier to navigate. The game also has a ridiculous amount of DLC, which can feel a bit overwhelming if you want to unlock everything. But honestly, even with the clunky menus and the steep learning curve, it's easily one of the best co-op shooters out there and you can easily sink hundreds of hours into it.

PAYDAY 2 is easily the best heist simulator on the market, offering an unforgettable co-op experience when played with a group of friends. The dual gameplay mechanics let you switch between tactical, quiet stealth and explosive, action-packed gunplay, giving every robbery immense replay value. Unfortunately, the game's biggest flaw is its widespread cheater problem in public lobbies, which drains all the fun out of random matches. It is a fantastic shooter worth playing, provided you stick to private lobbies with your squad to avoid game-breaking hackers.

PAYDAY 2 is one of those games that is best enjoyed with friends. Planning heists, working together to complete objectives, and choosing whether to go in stealth or loud can provide dozens, if not hundreds, of hours of fun. Even though the game is over a decade old, it's still incredibly enjoyable and easy to come back to.

One of its biggest strengths is the amount of content it offers. There are plenty of heists, weapons, and skill builds to experiment with, and every mission can be approached in different ways. The developers supported the game for many years, adding a huge amount of content that keeps the gameplay fresh and rewarding.

Of course, the game isn't perfect. New players may feel overwhelmed by the number of mechanics and DLCs, and collecting all of the additional content can become quite expensive. Even so, the core gameplay is so much fun that it's easy to spend hundreds of hours playing.

Overall, PAYDAY 2 is an outstanding co-op game that has stood the test of time. If you enjoy planning heists and playing with friends, this is definitely a game worth checking out.

My Rating: 8.5/10. One of the best co-op games ever made.

Payday 2 is a game with seemingly infinite content. The base game isn't terrible, but owning the DLCs will massively improve your experience. When you take into consideration that you can play over 50 heists (some with multiple days which just adds to the variety in the gameplay), but not only can you play all those heists, a lot of them are able to be completed in both loud and stealth giving you 2 main options on how to go about doing the heist.

Payday 2 also comes with 22 different heisters, all of which have their own voice lines, masks & weapons (you're obviously not required to use these but it adds more personality to the characters overall). 

Moving on from the heisters. When it comes to weapons and their customisability, you have many and I mean MANY options to choose from. You want to mow down cops with a golden minigun? You can do it! You want to bash the skull of those bulldozers with a giant spoon? We got that here too. Payday 2 has some very silly and funny weapons so it's perfect if you want to mess around with friends while murdering civs by hitting them with a wad of cash. 

There's also a lot of attachments/modifications you can do to your weapons. I'm talking akimbo shotguns with explosive ammo, a bow with poisoned arrows, a grenade launcher that shoots shocking grenades. 

There are over 200 weapons/weapon variations. These include, explosive weapons like an RPG, very powerful Sniper Rifles, Akimbo SMGs, Pistols & Shotguns, LMGs (or a minigun if you're feeling ballsy) and much more.

For those who love gun skins Payday 2 also has those, most of which look very clean (especially on mint-condition obviously). But if you think that skins for your guns is all that Payday 2 has to offer, you are dead wrong my friend. There are also armour skins which only your teammates can see it on you but still, it's there. There are "outfits" which technically aren't skins but I'm grouping them here cuz it works. Outfits change your characters default outfit, so…
A game with interesting strategy and in-depth loadout building wearing the mask (lol) of a mindless horde shooter. Have some friends on hand to make your initial hours less boring.
stealth is amazing, but you need the dlcs

Left 4 Dead but you rob people. + Stealth Play as well that's both challenging and fun. Great progression, not pay-to-win ftmp. Some DLC should be purchased but you can see what things are part of what DLC and each one is like $3. Great gameplay loop, and OFFLINE PLAY. Isn't THAT exciting in 2026? It will feel early on like your typical online game when you see continental coins, trust, these are NOT microtransactional, they exponentially become more available as you progress. The grind is deeply tied to the real, human pace of the game. Yes, you'll revisit or grind a few missions, but as you do, it's less "Oh let's get my numbers up" and more "I'm learning so much about this game, I'm going to be so much better at this next time." I slept on this one for years. Exceptional. You GOT to pay attention to the map sidebar. The tutorials, and the campaign are in there, as well as new modes you unlock once you've gotten competent enough. Career/Campaign really just ties the experience together for offline play and it's great to get slightly more challenge as you go. When you become able to finally fight in Mayhem difficulty, you will truly get that rush of a proper progression system.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the unmodded user interface and lack of built-in explanations create a steep learning curve requiring many hours to understand mechanics.

citations.review_text:
One of the best horde shooters out there, but instead of zombies you shoot cops.
Tons of content, almost a hundred heists, tens of valid character builds, over a thousand achievements that add another chunk of content if you decide to pursue them. One of the best hardcore communitys out there as well, most of people are really helpful and will gladly waste 4 hours with you trying to cook as much meth as they can. So even if you don't have friends to play with, you will find them here.

Music is great, gunplay is fun and satysfying, the heists are fun and memorable, designed in a way that you can do them tens of times and you won't get bored.

The game has a lot of (still supported and updated) mods, that veterans of this game can't play without anymore (like UI, HUD, QOL mods).

The game aged well, and despite being 13 years old still has tens of thousands monthly players. (Definitely doesn't have anything to do with payday 3 being a slop)

The biggest downside in my opinion is the learning curve. You need like a hundred hours to actually understand all mechanics, maps and develop good decision making. Or you need someone to walk you through the basics and more advanced stuff, cause the game is pretty bad at explaining anything and the unmodded UI will make new players really confused.

Pretty good game! It is coop pve only so no pvp! If you like to minmaxing and play different builds it has a depth with a lot of different guns and modifications. There is a talent tree with different branches for different playstyles and also perk decks with different stats and unique mechanics for your character. Decks are separate from talents but used in conjunction with talents and they create strong synergy.

You can build around your own playstyle and try different things. Make a different profiles and just switch around depending on what you want to play.

I recommend to start off with lower difficulties for couple of days to learn a game a little. There are 7 different difficulties.

You can do heists Loud or Stealth and both ways require different stats and build.
Most lobbies do Loud but when you search lobby you can toggle either Loud or Stealth which makes easier to find what you want.

A lot of things are locked behind DLC and honestly it is not a big deal because every gun has it's purpose and place. Being DLC gun does not mean 'better' automatically. Example is Mark-10 free SMG gun which is one of the best SMG in the game.

The only DLC i recommend to grab is Gage Mod Carrier. It contains bunch of different handy modifiers and it cost around 2 bucks. Mods are either unlocked or brought with in-game coins which are earned by just playing a game pretty much. These coins became useless after 100 hours of game time and i have 9 different builds so it is not grindy type of game at all.

Having around 30k-32k players daily at peak hours for a game this old speaks enough!
Also don't worry about meta ♥♥♥♥ unless you play the hardest difficulty. 
I play Death Wish mostly (second hardest) and honestly you can play any build you want while game remains challenging but not too sweaty. Game offers something for everybody!

Game is also getting updates even to this day and it is easy to hop in and hop out whenever you want. Even when you stop for a year and come b…
